title: LibConvert.abs(int256) underflows on type(int256).min via unchecked negation
description: abs(int256 a) returns `a >= 0 ? uint256(a) : uint256(-a)`. For a == type(int256).min, `-a` is not representable and the unary negation reverts under 0.8 checked arithmetic. abs() is applied to deltaB values (LibDeltaB.cappedReservesDeltaB / overallCappedDeltaB / calculateAgainstPeg / calculateTowardsPeg) and to overallConvertCapacity in pipelineConvert. deltaB is computed as `calcReserveAtRatioSwap(reserves) - reserves[beanIndex]`, bounded by realistic well reserve sizes (far below 2^255). I could not construct a reachable path producing int256.min, so this is a defensive/Info note rather than an exploitable finding.
impact: Theoretical revert (DoS) if a deltaB ever equalled type(int256).min; not reachable under realistic reserve magnitudes. No fund loss.

ite.intent: Revert convert penalty math via an abs() overflow
ite.technique: Supply deltaB == type(int256).min so uint256(-a) reverts
ite.evasion: Bounded by physical reserve sizes; not attacker-reachable
